direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale has a very indie feel, making it feel as if we are taking a seat in this apartment and watching a play as Wilde lets the actors play and build tension in this cramped apartment; The direction on a microscale works very well because everyone in this cast is able to work off each other to sell not only the amazing comedy but also the profoundness of the actual invite and how this polyamorous relationship represents a deeper dive into a failing marriage; The storytelling is strong because they are able to build a cringeworthy environment that makes you curl up in embarrassment, yet is so enjoyable that you really want to see what happens; Tension is built beautifully by the cringeworthiness of what is actually being said and happening on screen, which, coupled with the score, makes the overall movie a tense environment, as if you are in a pressure cooker waiting to explode

performance.comments: Incredibly a Seth Rogen role; he is basically playing the character he has played for the past 15 years—the studio Seth Rogen, the Neighbors Seth Rogen—and it fits him perfectly; it also helps that all the performances flow through him as he enables the chemistry and flow of comedy for the whole cast, especially Wilde

Surprisingly good in this movie; wearing the director's hat really allows her to shine because she knows exactly what she wants in the role as she is able to voice her frustrations of the relationship; has good chemistry with the cast, especially Rogen
Very much shows why she's won an Oscar; she is a great actress and her performance really shows it; has good chemistry with both Rogen and Norton

Shows his expertise and his experience as an actor in his scenes, especially delivering a very subtly strong monologue towards the end of the movie; while he isn't the most animated character in the movie, he shows the strength in subtlety as you really do feel for his character; has good chemistry with the whole cast, especially Cruz

cast.comments: There isn't a supporting cast for this movie, but the cast as a whole works so well because their incredible chemistry allows everybody to work off each other like they're improvising or riffing, creating a flow state of a movie

story.comments: The movie uses a simple concept of inviting neighbors over for dinner to explore themes of both polyamorous relationships and the failing marriage of the main couple; The plot structure is a pressure cooker, building up tension throughout the movie to make you cringe in your seat until it eventually explodes to show the state of these relationships; The character writing is strong, giving each of the four characters distinct perspectives and truths regarding their relationships and their lives

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is great, heavy, and so well-written that it creates a flow state where the actors build off each other, and you can definitely tell they were allowed to improvise as the characters build off each other to move the scenes forward; The humor is very funny, allowing jokes to pile on each other naturally with strong payoffs, where almost every single joke lands without feeling forced; It is very obvious that improvisation was used to help build jokes, especially when Seth Rogen is in the lead, as it helps create a flow state where everyone is able to build off each other to land the jokes; The symbolism is strong, subtly showing the state of a failing relationship, such as what they did with the hands and the piano in the last scene; The foreshadowing is strong, helping to hint at what is later revealed at the party, both about the visiting guests and the host couple

score.comments: The score is well woven in and accentuates the chaotic nature of the scenes to build tension and awkward comedy; However, while I understand that it is intentionally loud to help build this chaotic environment, it does get a little too loud at times, to the point where you cannot really hear what the characters are saying, so toning it down slightly would keep it loud while better accentuating the tension

soundtrack.comments: The soundtrack extends the score to help create and paint the vibe and tone of the movie

cinematography.comments: The movie is shot on film, which adds a wonderful, warm indie feel and great angles; The lighting is used brilliantly to accentuate truth and deception, such as when Seth Rogen's face is illuminated by a lamp to show he is telling the truth, whereas when Olivia Wilde dims the lights, it shows her hiding from the truth of her failing marriage

editing.comments: The movie is well-edited, which helps give it an indie and artistic feel

sound.comments: The sound is used very well for an indie movie to help build tension in the cramped apartment

production_design.comments: Considering this movie takes place in one apartment in the Bay Area, the filmmakers do a good job of giving it life while also making it feel filled with cluttered artistic elements to help show how trapped this couple feels, both artistically and in their relationship

review.pacing: The pacing is strong, moving neither too fast nor too slow; The constant riffing and relentless comedy keep things moving at just the right pace throughout
review.climax: The climax is very strong and profound, clearly showing where these couples are in their relationships and lives while weaving in well-crafted comedy; However, I felt the final shot of the movie hurt the film, as it could have been more profound if they had cut at a specific spot instead of keeping the camera running
review.tone: Tonally, it is pure comedy rather than a comedy-drama, as the characters are allowed to improvise and build off each other to constantly land jokes, yet it remains profound in its messaging by exploring polyamory and failing marriages in a comedic way
review.overall: Overall, 'The Invite' is a very good comedy that is the definition of being in a flow state; The movie's incredible chemistry and well-written dialogue, in conjunction with the freedom to improvise, allow the cast to bounce off each other to deliver hilarious comedy that also uncovers a profound story about polyamorous relationships and failing marriages
